title: [ORION-QG QG-26] Parikh-histogram kernel and finite guarded tropical regime geometry for all-n TARE
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Primary structural parent: QG-23 #879 / PR #882, protected GREEN auxiliary-support theorem (`|U_aux|<=6` all n).
Related parent: QG-24 #880 / PR #883 finite tropical weighted-automaton lane (independent route; QG-26 does not require QG-24 for its core histogram theorem).
Method donors: Parikh images, commutative automata/rational series, Presburger/semilinear geometry, tropical/min-plus piecewise-affine functions.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE COMMUTATIVE REGIME-GEOMETRY THEOREM — freeze before template enumeration/outcome.**

QG-23 earns that after the all-n QG-7c reductions there exists an optimum whose entire nontrivial auxiliary support

`U_aux = supp(Tag) union all frame-support / phantom-home coordinates`

has cardinality at most six. (For A/C, frame support is on Tag coordinates; for P, the only extra coordinate is its one Tag-free home.)

Outside `U_aux`, every frame and Tag letter is identity. Therefore Restore letters equal the target letters there, and the F3 contribution of a spectator coordinate is fixed once the global target-permutation tuple is fixed.

This suggests a stronger exact representation in **column-count space** rather than word/order space.

## Q1 — Parikh / histogram state

For a fixed matching, each qubit column is one type

`t in Sigma = {I,X,Y,Z}^6`, `|Sigma|=4096`.

Let `N_t` be the number of physical qubits with type t. The vector

`N=(N_t)_{t in Sigma} in N^4096`

is the Parikh/histogram image of the six-target instance.

Simultaneously permuting physical qubit coordinates does not change Pauli weights, symplectic products, the F3 rule, Tag/frame feasibility or the frozen unit objective. QG-26 must machine-bind this permutation invariance rather than assume it from terminology.

## Q2 — spectator baseline

For each of the 8 target-permutation tuples `pi`, define the exact linear spectator baseline

`B_pi(N) = sum_t N_t * b_pi(t)`,

where `b_pi(t)` is the two-branch F3 cost of target column type t when all six frame letters and the Tag letter are identity.

All `b_pi(t)` are integers derived from the frozen 64-entry F3 table. There are exactly 8 baseline coefficient vectors in `Z^4096`.

## Q3 — finite active templates

An **active template** tau records, up to permutation of active coordinates:
- one of the 8 target-permutation tuples;
- one of the 8 central-bit tuples;
- `k<=6` active column types (with multiplicity);
- on each active coordinate, six local frame letters plus one Tag letter;
- the accumulated six frame-support counts, three frame-pair symplectic parities and six Tag/frame syndrome parities;
- final exact R6M acceptance.

Require that every listed active coordinate actually contains at least one nonidentity auxiliary letter. Frames/Tag are identity on every unlisted coordinate.

Because `k<=6`, the target alphabet and local auxiliary alphabet are finite, the complete semantic template universe is finite and independent of physical n.

No claim is made that the explicit universe is small.

## Q4 — guarded affine cost of one template

For one accepted template tau with target-type multiplicities `m_tau(t)`, feasibility on histogram N is the finite threshold guard

`N_t >= m_tau(t)` for every t used by tau.

For every feasible N, tau has exact cost

`C_tau(N) = B_pi(N) + K_tau`,

where `K_tau` is an integer constant equal to:
- exact frame/Tag structural cost of the active auxiliary letters (including the frozen -18 offset), plus
- on each active coordinate, `F3_restore_with_aux - b_pi(target_type)`.

Thus each template contributes one affine function over an upward-closed integer guard region.

## Q5 — exact all-n finite guarded tropical representation

Prove both directions:

1. Every QG-23-normalized optimal configuration determines one accepted template tau of size <=6, so its cost is represented by `C_tau(N)`.
2. Every accepted template whose multiplicity guard is satisfied can be realized by assigning its active entries to distinct physical columns of the required types; the resulting full configuration is original-R6M admissible and has exactly `C_tau(N)`.

Therefore, on every valid six-target histogram,

`C_DP(N) = min_{tau feasible on N} [B_{pi(tau)}(N) + K_tau]`.

Equivalently, exact all-n TARE cost factors through the 4096-dimensional column histogram and is a **finite guarded tropical/min-affine function** of N.

This is the core QG-26 theorem.

## Q6 — exact regime cells in count space

Each template's guard is Presburger/semilinear (`N_t>=m_t`), and pairwise cost ties/dominance are integer affine inequalities because baselines are linear and corrections constant.

Hence the valid histogram cone admits a finite partition into exact integer polyhedral/semilinear cells on which one finite set of templates is optimal.

Candidate compiler-specific science:
- an all-n exact **count-space regime geometry**;
- finite template identities for every exact compiler regime;
- exact tie walls/multicritical cells in target-column-count space;
- a direct connection between QG-5/QG-5b forecasting and the complete (possibly enormous) template basis.

Generic Presburger/tropical cell decomposition receives zero novelty credit.

## Q7 — strong compression consequences

The theorem may state only:
- target qubit **order** is irrelevant; the histogram is sufficient;
- after an O(n) histogram pass, dependence on physical n enters only through the 4096 integer counts;
- the active auxiliary correction needs at most six selected histogram occurrences.

Do not claim a practical constant-time compiler without an explicit tractable template representation.

A successor may seek symmetry quotienting of the 4096 types or a compact generated template/test-set basis.

## Q8 — hostile controls

Mandatory controls:
- QG-7f's weight-3 overlapping comm-s2 configuration must be representable; no hidden common-two-coordinate assumption;
- QG-22/QG-7e show local environment information matters, so active target-column types must be retained exactly rather than collapsed to natural low-order features;
- spectator target contributions may depend on the global target permutation, hence all 8 baselines must remain distinct until machine equality proves otherwise.

## Independent generic ORION

Generic ORION must independently reconstruct phase-free Pauli/F3 algebra and verify:
- qubit-permutation invariance;
- the 8 spectator baseline vectors;
- template cost decomposition on a frozen exhaustive small template domain;
- histogram-realization bijection for serialized templates;
- no dependence on physical coordinate identities remains after type/multiplicity replacement.

It need not enumerate the complete astronomical template universe to prove finiteness; it must prove the finite bound and decomposition structurally.

## Native ORION-Q

Keep distinct:
- `HISTOGRAM_SUFFICIENT_STATISTIC_ALL_N`;
- `FINITE_GUARDED_TROPICAL_TEMPLATE_REPRESENTATION`;
- `EXPLICIT_TEMPLATE_BASIS_ENUMERATED`;
- `PRACTICAL_STATIC_FORECASTER`;
- `CLOSED_FORM_BDOUBLEPRIME_COMPLETENESS`;
- `CHAIN_ALL_N`.

Only the first two are candidate V1 authorities.

## Strong intended terminal

`QG26_TARE_EXACT_COST_IS_FINITE_GUARDED_TROPICAL_FUNCTION_OF_4096_COLUMN_COUNTS_ALL_N`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG26_QG23_AUX_SUPPORT_BINDING_GAP`
- `QG26_SPECTATOR_BASELINE_NOT_AFFINE__MISSING_COUPLING`
- `QG26_HISTOGRAM_REALIZATION_COUNTEREXAMPLE`
- `QG26_GENERIC_NATIVE_DISAGREEMENT`
- `QG26_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Donor subtraction / novelty boundary

Parikh images, commutative monoids, rational/weighted series, Presburger arithmetic, semilinear sets, tropical polynomials and finite min-affine decompositions are established theory and receive zero novelty credit. Candidate contribution is only the exact TARE-specific all-n histogram sufficiency theorem, six-active-column correction structure, and resulting compiler regime geometry. No R6 or physical quantum-advantage authority is requested.
